title.narrative: 4.2 Development and establishment of Parliamentary Institute

description.narrative: 4.2 Development and establishment of Parliamentary Institute

comment.narrative: The SAPI was successfully launched on Thursday 9 December 2021 in Parliament Cape Town by the SALS under the leadership of the Speakers Forum. The institute is intended to enhance the functioning of Parliament and the nine legislatures by providing capacity development programmes for Members of Parliament and Provincial Legislatures produce timely and quality research and knowledge management for the Legislative Sector. Amongst others the hybrid event launch was attended by executive authority of Parliament Members of the Speakers Forum House Chairpersons Chair of Chairs of the Provincial Legislatures Whips of Parliament and Legislatures board of the Parliamentary Institute international guests including EU Ambassador and delegates from the education sector and legislative sector partners. The roles and functions of the institute includes the design development and implementation of capacity building programmes for staff and members conduct quality research and provide uptodate information to members of the Legislatures and its committees provide advice and technical assistance to committees and office bearers in the legislative and policy related matters establish and host an alumni association of the Sector former MPsMPLs and Officials.The Institute is governed by a Board of 11 qualified members with expertise in parliamentary practice public policy teaching and learning as well as finance and business matters. The Board is accountable to the Speakers Forum and will serve for a period of 5 years parliamentary term and will oversee the implementation of the existing Sector programmes and expand with new programmes. It will begin its work by developing a strategy for the Institute SAPI conduct consultations and create awareness about the role of the Institute to all Sector stakeholders and develop programme frameworks based on the pillars of the institute. Following the launch of the Parliamentary Institute the board members held their first meeting which focused on the induction of board members on their roles and responsibilities and used the meeting to identify high level priorities for establishment and the implementation of the institute in this term. Based on the action plan the following baseline documents were developed and actioned Board charter developed board committees established the strategy framework for the institute was developed the information brochure on role and functions of institute was developed and circulated.
